title: Why aren't you at school?
setting: A morning at home. Yuki is dressed for work and about to head out when she finds her little brother Kenji still lounging around the house.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenji, mada uchi ni iru no? gakkou wa?
lines.ja: ケンジ、まだうちにいるの？学校は？
lines.kana: けんじ、まだうちにいるの？がっこうは？
lines.english: Kenji, you're still home? What about school?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: うん。今日は学校行かない。
lines.kana: うん。きょうはがっこういかない。
lines.english: Yeah. I'm not going to school today.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, nande? minna mou gakkou itteru yo.
lines.ja: え、なんで？みんなもう学校行ってるよ。
lines.kana: え、なんで？みんなもうがっこういってるよ。
lines.english: What? Why not? Everyone else is already at school.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: nee-chan wa? kyou shigoto iku no?
lines.ja: 姉ちゃんは？今日仕事行くの？
lines.kana: ねえちゃんは？きょうしごといくの？
lines.english: What about you, sis? You're going to work today?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: iku yo. shigoto metcha isogashii no.
lines.ja: 行くよ。仕事めっちゃ忙しいの。
lines.kana: いくよ。しごとめっちゃいそがしいの。
lines.english: Of course I am. Work's crazy busy.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: fuun. shigoto nanji ni owaru no?
lines.ja: ふーん。仕事何時に終わるの？
lines.kana: ふーん。しごとなんじにおわるの？
lines.english: Huh. What time do you get off?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: juuji kana. kinou mo shigoto, juuji ni owatta shi.
lines.ja: 10時かな。昨日も仕事、10時に終わったし。
lines.kana: じゅうじかな。きのうもしごと、じゅうじにおわったし。
lines.english: Ten, probably. I didn't get off till ten yesterday either.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: 大変だね。でも、姉ちゃん。
lines.kana: たいへんだね。でも、ねえちゃん。

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. dakara gakkou ikanai n da yo.
lines.ja: うん。だから学校行かないんだよ。
lines.kana: うん。だからがっこういかないんだよ。
lines.english: Yeah. That's why I'm not going to school.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, okaasan wa? shigoto itteru n ja nai no?
lines.ja: じゃあ、お母さんは？仕事行ってるんじゃないの？
lines.kana: じゃあ、おかあさんは？しごといってるんじゃないの？
lines.english: Then what about Mom? Isn't she at work?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: ううん、買い物行ってるだけ。
lines.kana: ううん、かいものいってるだけ。

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, honto da. jaa, watashi mo shigoto ikanakute ii n da!
lines.ja: あ、ほんとだ。じゃあ、私も仕事行かなくていいんだ！
lines.kana: あ、ほんとだ。じゃあ、わたしもしごといかなくていいんだ！
lines.english: Oh, it really is Saturday! So I don't have to go to work either!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: 姉ちゃん、仕事忙しすぎだよ。
lines.kana: ねえちゃん、しごといそがしすぎだよ。
lines.english: Sis, your job keeps you way too busy.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: da yo ne. jaa kenji, kaimono iku?
lines.ja: だよね。じゃあケンジ、買い物行く？
lines.kana: だよね。じゃあけんじ、かいものいく？
lines.english: Tell me about it. Okay, Kenji, want to go shopping?

choices.english: Yuki is about to leave for work when Kenji points out that it's Saturday: no school for him, and no work for her.
Kenji is skipping school, so Yuki makes him go before she leaves for work.
Yuki's work finishes early today, so she asks Kenji to go shopping with her after work.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-3: Yuki finds Kenji still at home and thinks he's skipping school. Lines 4-7: she's off to work, it's busy, and she expects to get off around ten. Line 10: kyou, doyoubi da yo (it's Saturday). Line 12: that's why he isn't going to school, and line 14: Mom isn't at work, she's just out shopping. Line 15: so Yuki doesn't have to go to work either (shigoto ikanakute ii n da). B is wrong: Kenji never goes, because there's no school on a Saturday. C is wrong: Yuki has no work at all today; she asks Kenji to go shopping right now (line 17), and he says no and goes back to bed (line 18: uun. oyasumi).

questions.english: When Yuki finds Kenji at home, she tells him "minna mou gakkou itteru yo." Where does she say everyone else is?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、みんなが今どこにいると言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、みんながいまどこにいるといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, minna ga ima doko ni iru to iimashita ka?

choices.english: On their way to school right now.
At home, just about to leave for school.

questions.explanation: Line 3: gakkou itteru is the -teru form of iku, the state after going: they went and are there now, and mou (already) backs that up. A is wrong: on the way would be gakkou iku tochuu (or gakkou ni mukatteru), never itteru. B is wrong: about to leave is plain iku, as in ima kara gakkou iku. The same -teru state comes back in lines 13-14, where Yuki asks if Mom is at work (shigoto itteru n ja nai no?) and Kenji says she's out shopping (kaimono itteru dake). Elsewhere gakkou itteru can also mean 'attends school' (nihongo gakkou itteru: I go to a Japanese school).

questions.english: One weekday morning Kenji sees you heading for the door and asks, "a, mou deru no? doko iku no?" (Oh, you're leaving already? Where are you going?) You're off to work. Tell him.
questions.ja: あ、もう出るの？どこ行くの？
questions.kana: あ、もうでるの？どこいくの？
questions.romaji: a, mou deru no? doko iku no?
questions.answer: Say you're going to work, with shigoto and plain iku: shigoto iku yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: ima kara shigoto itte kuru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 今から仕事行ってくるね。
modelAnswers.english: I'm off to work now. See you later.

questions.explanation: Heading off is plain iku: shigoto iku yo, the way Kenji asks in line 4 (kyou shigoto iku no?) and Yuki answers in line 5 (iku yo). itte kuru, 'go and come back', is the everyday I'm-off line. Don't say shigoto itteru here: that's the state, already at work, which is how Yuki asks about Mom in line 13 (shigoto itteru n ja nai no?). Casual speech drops ni; politely it's shigoto ni ikimasu.

questions.english: Kenji asks Yuki a 'what time' question about her work. What did he ask?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: What time will you get the job done?
choices.romaji: nanji ni shigoto o owaraseru no?

choices.english: What time do you get off work?
What time do you go to work?

questions.explanation: Line 6: shigoto nanji ni owaru no? For getting off work, the work itself ends: shigoto is the subject of owaru (with ga, dropped in casual speech), even though English says 'you finish'. A is the word-for-word 'you finish work': owaraseru means making something finish, so it's about getting a task done, not clocking off. C asks when she goes in (iku); Yuki is already heading out, and her answer is about the end of her day: juuji kana, kinou mo shigoto, juuji ni owatta shi (line 7).

questions.english: Yuki says to you, "kinou mo kaeri osokatta ne. nande?" (You got home late again yesterday. How come?) It's because work has been busy. Tell her.
questions.ja: 昨日も帰り遅かったね。なんで？
questions.kana: きのうもかえりおそかったね。なんで？
questions.romaji: kinou mo kaeri osokatta ne. nande?
questions.answer: Give work as the reason, with shigoto as the subject of isogashii: shigoto isogashii n da yo.

modelAnswers.english: Yeah, work's just been so busy.

questions.explanation: English says 'I've been busy with work'; Japanese makes the work the subject: shigoto (ga) isogashii, as Yuki says in line 5 (shigoto metcha isogashii no) and Kenji in line 16 (shigoto isogashisugi da yo). The -kute form, shigoto ga isogashikute, trails off as the reason and is the standard excuse. Keep isogashii for people and their work or schedule: a crowded shop is konderu, not isogashii.

newWords.english: sis (what a younger sibling calls a big sister)
tough, rough (taihen da ne = that's rough)
just, only (kaimono itteru dake = she's just out shopping)
too, too much (isogashisugi = way too busy)
say (nan to iimashita ka = what did they say?)
